text:
Cold email: "We noticed your website has ranking issues. We can get you to page one."

Google's own guide on hiring an SEO compares unsolicited SEO emails to spam.

The good ones are usually too busy looking after clients to be spraying out cold emails.

Straight to the bin.

Leave last Boxing Day's sale sign in the shop window.
Then hire a keen new casual who reads it out to every customer.

That's Google Ads automated promotions on a website full of old specials.

He's just doing his job. You'd still want a word with him.

Running a Christmas special in your Google Ads?

Add the promotion yourself. Your words, your terms, a start date and an end date.

An electrician in Chermside can run a December safety check offer, end it on the 24th, and sleep fine.

Then Google stops guessing.

Who looks after your Google Business Profile?

If the answer is three staff and an old agency login nobody remembers, that's nobody.

Pick one person. They check it weekly, read Google's emails and notice when a post gets knocked back.

Worth sorting this week.

When you call me, you get me.

No salespeople. No closers. No scripts.

If I think I can help, I'll tell you. If I don't, I'll tell you that too.

Simple.

A physio in Fitzroy runs Google Ads with her clinic address showing under the ad. No promotion of her own.

That's the exact setup Google switched automated promotions on for from October 12. On by default. Nobody ticked a box.

Does your account look like hers?
